title: The Evolutionary Raw Deal of the Human Knee - Nautilus
gist: Humans, despite evolving to spend much time on their feet, have poorly designed knees, while great apes lack similar knee problems — and a new Nature study says the difference has nothing to do with apes' arboreal lifestyle.

insights.claim: For a species that evolved to spend so much time standing and walking, humans have remarkably poorly designed knee joints, commonly experienced as crackling and nagging pain.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Structural knee vulnerability underpins durable demand for orthopedics and joint-replacement markets.
insights.quote: we have remarkably poorly designed joints in our legs

insights.claim: Great apes do not have the same knee problems as humans.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Comparative anatomy may reveal the evolutionary cause of human joint disease.

insights.claim: According to a new study in Nature, great apes' freedom from human-style knee problems has nothing to do with their arboreal lifestyle, contradicting an intuitive explanation.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Reframes the evolutionary basis of knee disease, potentially relevant to osteoarthritis research.
insights.quote: it’s got nothing to do with their arboreal lifestyle
